reason: While the text depicts Israelites complaining to Moses about their circumstances and Moses encouraging them toward faith and silence ('תַּחֲרִישׁוּן' - hold your peace), the primary moral emphasis of this passage (Exodus 14) is on God's power and faithfulness in delivering His people, not on the wrongness of complaining to leaders. The narrative focuses on trust in divine salvation rather than on condemning the act of complaint itself. Moses responds to the people's fear with encouragement toward faith and divine deliverance, not with a rebuke of complaint as inherently improper.
